scalars.scalar_value: Experience working in a research laboratory environment

items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Physiology, Neuroscience, Molecular Biology, or related scientific field
Experience working in a research laboratory environment
Experience with tissue processing, histology, cell culture, immunostaining, or related laboratory techniques

The Department of Orthopedic Surgery is seeking a part-time Laboratory Assistant II to support research in our laboratory. The laboratory focuses on skeletal muscle dysfunction, musculoskeletal regeneration, fibrosis, cerebral palsy, and related neuromuscular disorders. Key responsibilities include:
Assist with human muscle and small animal tissue research, including tissue collection, cryopreservation, processing, and histological analyses
Perform immunostaining procedures, microscopy, image acquisition, and quantitative image analysis
Support studies related to stem cells and musculoskeletal regeneration
Maintain mammalian tissue and cell cultures and prepare laboratory reagents, chemical solutions, and buffers
Organize and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies, records, and inventory
Coordinate and maintain laboratory equipment, supplies, records, and inventory
Coordinate laboratory maintenance activities, equipment servicing, procurement, and installation
Ensure compliance with laboratory safety regulations and proper handling and disposal of biological and chemical materials
Assist with research data organization, quality control, analysis, and record management
Support preparation of research reports, scientific presentations, manuscripts, and grant-related materials
Please note: this is a limited position that may convert to career
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and basic data management tools

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Ability to operate and maintain laboratory equipment, including microscopes, cryostats, and imaging software
Knowledge of standard biochemical laboratory procedures and laboratory best practices
Knowledge of mammalian tissue culture techniques and preparation of laboratory best practices
Working knowledge of laboratory safety regulations and the handling and disposal of biological and chemical materials
Strong organizational skills with the ability to maintain accurate laboratory records and inventory
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Ability to complete all required UCLA research and safety training
